_comment: What the golden-screenshot gate covers. Driven by scripts/golden_screens.py.
Every screen here is deliberately STATIC at the capture point -- a title
screen or a menu waiting for input -- so that the instruction-count capture
point lands on the same picture on a fast host and a slow one. A screen that
is animating cannot be a golden without a tolerance so wide it stops being a
'insns' is guest_insns_total: the deterministic capture point. 'tolerance' is
a per-channel value, and 'max_diff_pct' the fraction of pixels allowed past
it. Both are 0 for a screen that should be bit-identical; anything non-zero
needs a reason recorded next to it.

ALLEYCAT.mask_reason: Two bands, both driven by guest TIME rather than by the instruction stream, so no instruction-count capture point can freeze them. (1) y=108..134: the cat sprite walks the fence off the PIT tick, and two runs at the same guest_insns_total put it 30-55 px apart. (2) y=200..222: the copyright line CYCLES between '(C) Copyright IBM Corp. 1984' and '(C) Copyright SynSoft(TM) 1984' on a timer -- a capture is a coin flip between two equally correct screens. Differences inside both bands are still counted and printed; everything else -- title text, fence, dustbins, the words painted on it, palette -- gates exactly.
